item.description: Local volunteer attorneys offer free legal information and referral for matters of family law only. These lawyer consultations will last up to 20 minutes. Sign-ups are first come, first served in person and begin at 10 am. \(30 minutes before the program begins\) The attorneys are volunteers and provide only legal information. They do not provide specific legal advice and should not be considered as personal lawyers for any reason. You will be required to sign a waiver before speaking to an attorney that states that no attorney-client relationship is being created with this free service. No language translation services or interpreters are offered or provided by library staff. Participants must bring their own interpreter if one is needed. Participants may also bring support persons, family members or other affiliated persons to meet with the attorney together. item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Oct 15, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: Bongs + Books Silent Book Club at The Lounge at Mercy — Fri Oct 16, 5:00 PM — The Lounge at Mercy
item.description:
Bongs \+ Books is our monthly silent book club where we light up & swap small talk for story time. No assigned books, no deadlines, no discussions or small talk — just a shared space to unwind, light up, and get lost in a good read.
Bring whatever you’re currently reading \(or listening - we have coloring books and puzzles for our audiobook lovers!\), grab something to smoke, and settle in for a cozy, low-pressure night of uninterrupted reading alongside fellow book lovers.
Come solo or with friends and enjoy comfy vibes, good weed, and a room full of people happily minding their own business.
How it works:
5-6pm: Arrive, get settled, and kick things off with a short welcome sesh.
6-7pm: heads-down reading time, lo-fi music, and chill energy.
7-8pm: wrap up chapters, meet other readers, one last sesh to end the evening!
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.description:

item.description:
The Sonoma County Genealogical Society Presents
Using AI to Bring Your Presentation to Life
Presented by Jane Pritchard
Jane will present the slide show she created for the Santa Rosa Chapter of the DAR honoring her Revolutionary War patriot, Margaret Eskridge Kenner, who supported Revolutionary troops with food and supplies. Along the way she taught herself to use AI assistants Claude and Nano Banana, to speed up research and to build both the PowerPoint and a companion PDF. She will walk through the simple, practical ways she used AI — and where it fell short so members can try the same approach with their own ancestors.
Jane began serious family research in 2021, during the pandemic, and has since taken many genealogy classes through Santa Rosa Junior College. item.title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.
The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.
